title: Receive supplier order files over SFTP and acknowledge them
summary: When a supplier uploads an order CSV file, the integration waits until the upload is complete, checks the contents, avoids processing it twice, stores it and tells the supplier the result.

requirements.text: Receive CSV order files through SFTP
Only process a file after its upload has finished
Check columns, required fields and values
Never process the same file twice
requirements.note: What counts as 'the same' needs detail

requirements.text: Store accepted files and set aside invalid ones
Use Azure to run the integration

outcomes: A half-uploaded file is never processed.
Uploading the same file again does not create a second order.
Invalid files are set aside with a clear reason.
The acknowledgement only says what really happened at the agreed point.
example: orders-042.csv is uploaded, then orders-042.ready appears. The file passes the checks and is stored as accepted. Uploading it again is recorded as a duplicate. A broken file is set aside and the supplier gets a rejection.

steps.title: Supplier uploads a file
steps.text: Plus a 'ready' marker, or a rename when the upload is done.

steps.title: We wait until it's complete
steps.text: And check we haven't seen this file before.

steps.title: We check the contents
steps.text: Columns, required fields and values, against the agreed layout.

steps.title: We store the result
steps.text: Accepted files in one place, invalid files set aside with the reason.

steps.title: The supplier gets an answer
steps.text: Only after the outcome is safely recorded.

suggestion: Start with one Logic App, file storage and a small 'already processed' record. Add more pieces only if volumes or outages require them.

main.name: Logic App
main.text: Waits for complete files, checks them, avoids duplicates

flow.text: The workflow picks up a complete file from SFTP.
The supplier gets an acceptance or a rejection with the reason.

architecture.note: Whether the SFTP server is the supplier's, ours, or Azure's own SFTP decides the connection (question 1).

key_rule.title: The key rule: never process an incomplete or repeated file

items.label: Incomplete
items.text: orders-043.csv without its .ready marker: wait, don't process.

items.label: Valid
items.text: Marker present, checks pass, file not seen before: process once.

items.label: Duplicate
items.text: Same supplier and same file identity: record it, don't create another order.

items.label: Invalid
items.text: Wrong layout or missing data: set aside and report why.

protections.title: No half-written files
protections.text: We only read a file once its upload is confirmed complete.

protections.title: No duplicate orders
protections.text: A processed-file record stops the same file being handled twice.

protections.title: No false 'success'
protections.text: The acknowledgement only means what we agreed, nothing more.

protections.title: No lost files
protections.text: Failed and set-aside files can be found and reprocessed.

questions.title: Where is the SFTP server?
questions.why: It decides how Azure connects and how it's secured.
questions.tech: Host type, authentication method, inbound or outbound connection, VNet/gateway needs

questions.title: How do suppliers show an upload is finished?
questions.why: Reading a half-uploaded file can corrupt an order.
questions.tech: Finalisation contract, file naming pattern, atomic rename support

questions.title: Where should valid orders go?
questions.why: Storing a file is different from creating orders in a business system.
questions.tech: Target interface, schema, persistence and transaction boundary

questions.title: What counts as the same file?
questions.why: Two files with the same name can hold different orders.
questions.tech: Idempotency key, replay window, conflict handling

questions.title: When should the supplier get an acknowledgement?
questions.why: Receiving a file is not the same as processing it successfully.

notes: A durable processed-file record and audit trail stop replays from creating the same order twice.
Failures before the acknowledgement point must never report success.
Use scoped credentials and Key Vault; keep file contents out of logs and acknowledgements.
Unknowns: SFTP location, completion convention, file layout, target system, duplicate key, acknowledgement meaning, volumes.

glossary.meaning: A secure way to upload and download files.
The message telling the supplier whether their file was accepted.
A file we have already processed.
